why: INTERNAL, not user API -- the header says 'Not intended for user code'. It parks the closure BLOCK on the `Timer` AFTER the runtime has registered a raw `void(*)(void*)` pointing into that same block, so the closure outlives the registration and is freed when the timer is destroyed or moved from. rclcpp needs no equivalent because `rclcpp::TimerBase` owns its callback object directly; our runtime callback is a C function pointer, so the closure needs an owner on this side. UNCONDITIONAL since phase-442 W1 (issue 1225), and that is the point: it takes a `detail::HostedBlockBase*` and stores it in an unconditional `void*`, because the MEMBER may not follow a capability probe -- a `sizeof(nros::Timer)` of 24 or 32 depending on a flag one module of an image may set on its own is issue 0135's class. The block's ALLOCATION lived in `std_compat.hpp`, which phase-442 W2 DELETED; W3 gives the member its next writer. It was already in this report before it became unconditional, because the extractor compiles a `-DNROS_CPP_STD=1` translation unit (issue 0818) and `public_surface`'s not-public-API filter is applied to the ROS 2 side only, so an `@internal` of ours has nowhere to be excluded. `cpp:GuardCondition::attach_closure_block` is its twin.
